newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - December 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - December 26.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Thursday's edition of Daily Variety:
HOLLYWOOD - A Morality in Media study says that advertiser support for so-called "trash talk" television is on the decline and that several talkers have also started to clean up their act.
WASHINGTON - Broadcasters have taken the nation's largest satellite carrier to federal court, charging that PrimeTime 24 was illegally selling access to network feeds to DBS subscribers.
HOLLYWOOD - NBC, a subsidiary of General Electric Co, won a week filled with Christmas specials and holiday-themed programming, taking households as well as the 18-49, 25-54 and 18-34 demographics.

HOLLYWOOD - While Yuletime traditionally is a box office bonanza, not everyone is celebrating this year. Some pricey films are foundering, and even some of the season's more successful titles may fall short of the benchmark $100 million domestic level.
TORONTO - Livent Inc is reporting record ticket sales for Ragtime, the Musical, which is headed for an L.A. stand in advance of its Broadway opening.

HOLLYWOOD - In the TV industry's latest battle against its biggest enemy -- the remote control -- producers and networks are coming up with new tricks to cut down on channel surfing. That means getting rid of anything routine or boring.
